title: Initial data loads (customers, vendors, costCodes) swallow errors silently
detail: Lines 239-241: three parallel fetches (fetchCustomers, fetchVendors, fetchCostCodes) each have `.catch(() => {})` — empty catch blocks. If any of these fail (e.g. network issue, 403), the user gets an empty customer picker / vendor drawer / cost code dropdown with zero feedback. Unlike MsaComposer (where Phase 2b added toasts for similar catches), ContractComposer was not touched because it was a newer file.
evidence: fetchCustomers().then(r => setCustomers(r?.value || [])).catch(() => {}); fetchVendors().then(r => setAllVendors(r?.value || [])).catch(() => {}); fetchCostCodes().then(r => setCostCodes(r?.value || [])).catch(() => {});
recommendedFix: Add toast.show('err', 'Failed to load customers/vendors/cost codes') in each catch block. Follow the pattern established by MsaComposer post-CR-0401 fix.

title: Customer-change cascading loads swallow errors silently
detail: Lines 344-354: when customerId changes, five fetches fire (fetchLocationsByCustomer, fetchContractsByCustomer, fetchCustomerApMappings, fetchKnownVendorsByCustomer). Each has a .catch that silently sets empty state. If any one fails, the user sees empty dropdowns/drawers with no error indication — they may think the customer has no locations.
recommendedFix: Add toast.show('err', ...) to each catch. The existing pattern of resetting to empty state is correct (graceful degradation), but the user needs a visible signal that data is missing due to an error vs. genuinely absent.

title: resumeDraft has two empty catch blocks — errors are invisible
detail: Lines 578 and 590: two separate try/catch blocks inside resumeDraft have completely empty catch bodies (`catch {}`). If the detail GET or line-items fetch fails, the user sees a partially hydrated draft with no indication that data is missing. They might proceed to generate a document with stale/incomplete line items.
evidence: Line 578: `} catch {}` after apiGet for signer fields. Line 590: `} catch {}` after fetchContractLines.
recommendedFix: At minimum, toast.show('warn', 'Some draft data could not be loaded') in each catch. The user should know their resume was partial.

title: Signer inputs in inline panel have no associated labels or aria-labels
detail: Lines 816-822: four <input> elements for customer/vendor signer name and title use placeholder text only ('Full name', 'Title') with no <label>, htmlFor, aria-label, or aria-labelledby. Screen readers will announce these as unlabelled text inputs. The date picker input (line 806) also lacks a label element. For external user testing, sighted users can read the placeholder, but accessible users cannot.
recommendedFix: Add aria-label attributes: aria-label="Customer signer full name", aria-label="Customer signer title", aria-label="Vendor signer full name", aria-label="Vendor signer title". Same for the date input: aria-label="Contract date".

title: Customer search input in empty state has no associated label
detail: Line 948: the customer search <input> has a placeholder but no <label>, htmlFor, or aria-label. The surrounding <h2> asks 'Who is this Work Order for?' but is not programmatically associated with the input. Same issue affects the drawer search input at line 1166.
evidence: <input autoFocus type="text" placeholder="Type to search customers..." ... />
recommendedFix: Add aria-label="Search customers" to the empty-state input. Add aria-label to the drawer search input as well ("Search vendors" or "Search locations" based on drawer type).

title: Drawer overlay backdrop lacks aria attributes and focus trap
detail: Line 1153: the drawer overlay div is a click-to-dismiss backdrop with no role, aria-label, or keyboard handling beyond the global Escape listener. Focus can tab behind the drawer into the main page. For keyboard-only users, focus management is incomplete — though the keyboard nav effect (line 265) handles arrow keys and Escape within the drawer, it does not trap focus.
evidence: <div onClick={() => setDrawer(null)} style={{ position: 'fixed', inset: 0, background: 'rgba(0,0,0,0.25)', zIndex: 45 }} />
recommendedFix: Add role="dialog" and aria-modal="true" to the drawer container. Add aria-label="Close drawer" and role="button" to the backdrop. Consider a simple focus trap (tabindex=-1 on the container + autoFocus on the search input, which is already present).

title: Make button is not disabled during document generation — only visually styled
detail: Line 857-864: The floating 'Make the Work Order' button uses `disabled={missing.length > 0 || generating || !!docResult}` which correctly disables during generation. However, the handleGenerate function also returns early on `generating` (line 634), providing double-protection. The issue is that the button text says 'Making...' but there is no spinner or progress indicator — for a 30-second polling operation, the user has no visual confirmation that work is happening. The docResult slot (line 1117) shows 'Still generating' only after generation completes but doc URL polling continues.
evidence: Line 717-733: polling loop waits up to 30 seconds (6 iterations x 5s) with no progress update visible to the user except the button text 'Making...'.
recommendedFix: Add a status message or spinner below the Make button during generation, similar to MsaComposer's downloadStatus pattern. E.g., setDownloadStatus('Creating contract record...'), 'Generating document...', 'Waiting for SharePoint link...'.

title: DocGen polling uses $filter instead of direct GET by ID
detail: Line 723: `apiGet('/${EntitySets.documentRequests}?$filter=dcfg_document_requestid eq ${reqId}&$select=dcfg_status,dcfg_output_file_url')` — uses a $filter query to locate a record whose ID is already known. Should use a direct GET by key: `/${EntitySets.documentRequests}(${reqId})?$select=...`. The filter-based approach is less efficient and could theoretically return stale results if the portal API caches list queries differently from single-record GETs.
recommendedFix: Change to direct GET: apiGet(`/${EntitySets.documentRequests}(${reqId})?$select=dcfg_status,dcfg_output_file_url,dcfg_error_message`). Also add dcfg_error_message to the $select (it is checked on line 726-equivalent but not selected). Compare with MsaComposer line 343 which uses the correct direct-GET pattern.

title: WIP drafts load has empty catch — user won't know if draft resume failed
detail: Line 260: `fetchMyWIPDrafts(userEmail).then(...).catch(() => {})` — if the drafts query fails, the user won't see the resume landing even if they have drafts. Silent failure. The empty catch hides a potentially important feature from the user.
recommendedFix: Add toast.show('warn', 'Could not load saved drafts') in the catch.
